subject: LyricX throughput allocation plan, SLA match & fallback playbook

Subject: Initial sizing ask — production traffic shape and SLOs

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the demo this week — got good alignment on integration. To move the Dedicated quote forward we need a short traffic snapshot and your target SLOs so our infra team can produce a committed-capacity proposal. Could you confirm the following by end of day?

- Typical daily throughput (avg tokens/day) and your expected peak hour QPS for chat endpoints.
- Average and 95th percentile response length in tokens (so we can model tokens/sec).
- Required p95 latency SLO and any hard tail limits (e.g., p99 max).
- Any quiet-hour windows where you expect <20% load (useful for autoscaling proposals).

I've attached a simple spreadsheet that accepts your numbers and will output a recommended slab (GPU count/sku) with a conservative 30% burst cushion. If you prefer, we can run a short synthetic replay with your sample payloads — engineering says ~48 hours to collect a robust profile.

Goal: have a recommended committed slab and SLA draft by EOW so procurement can review.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — production traffic shape and SLOs

Kimberly — thanks, and appreciate the spreadsheet. Quick answers below (happy to share fuller logs if needed):

- Avg daily tokens: ~27M tokens/day (user messages + assistant tokens).
- Peak-hour QPS (chat endpoint): 48 QPS sustained for the busiest hour (we see short spikes up to ~85 QPS for a few minutes during product updates).
- Average response length: 180 tokens; p95 response length: 420 tokens.
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end < 350 ms for the chat generate call; p99 preferred < 800 ms but not blocking at launch.
- Quiet hours: PST 02:00–05:00 typically under 15% of peak.

We are planning to start with the rw-infer-v2-13b variant (quantized), but can fall back to a smaller distilled variant for non-critical paths.

Samir
CTO, LyricX

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: LyricX traffic — sizing sketch (internal)

Internal calc (quick sketch) — assumptions and conservative safety buffers below.

Assumptions:
- Model: rw-infer-v2-13b (q4f16 quantized path). We benchmarked this variant on H100 80GB in our testbed.
- Typical response (avg) = 180 tokens, p95 response = 420 tokens (Samir).
- Peak short spikes: 85 QPS for a few minutes. Peak sustained hour: 48 QPS.
- Measured per-H100 throughput (quantized): ~9,000 tokens/sec for mixed chat workload with warmed KV cache. Cold starts/cold KV windows: throughput drops; effective tokens/sec ~6,000 for first few minutes per replica.
- Latency model: per-token generation latency ~2.5–3.5 ms on H100 (warmed); end-to-end overhead (network + routing + batching) adds ~40–70 ms depending on concurrency. Our p95 target is 350 ms.

Calculations:
- Peak tokens/sec (p95 length): 85 QPS * 420 tokens = 35,700 tokens/sec (short spikes)
- Sustained peak tokens/sec (hour): 48 QPS * 420 tokens = 20,160 tokens/sec

Capacity math (warmed cache):
- Warm H100 capacity = 9,000 tps -> GPUs needed for sustained peak = ceil(20,160 / 9,000) = 3 GPUs
- Warm GPUs needed for short spikes = ceil(35,700 / 9,000) = 4 GPUs

Accounting for warm/cold mix and safety cushion:
- Cold-warm penalty: factor ~1.5 on tokens/sec for first N minutes per replica -> use effective capacity 6,000 tps per GPU to be safe for rollout/start-of-hour spikes.
- Safety buffer for network variance and OS-level jitter: +25%

Adjusted numbers (conservative):
- Sustained-hour planning: ceil(20,160 / 6,000 * 1.25) = ceil(3.36 * 1.25) -> effectively 5 GPUs reserve for predictable SLA-backed capacity.
- Short-spike headroom: ceil(35,700 / 6,000 * 1.25) = ceil(5.95) -> 6 GPUs to absorb short spikes without dropping to fallback.

Recommendation (Dedicated slab):
- Offer: 6x H100 80GB-equivalent reserved instances (slab). Rationale: meets short spike headroom (85 QPS peaks), supports warmed KV cache for majority of traffic, and leaves ~10–15% spare for internal backstop.
- Canary day 0: roll 10% traffic on slab, keep hosted fallback route for other 90% (auto-fallthrough). Increase to 50% day 1, then 100% when metrics stable (~48 hours).
- Fallbacks: automatic spill to smaller quantized model (rw-infer-v2-7b-q4) if slab consumed >95% for >2 minutes; additional overflow to hosted capacity for bursts longer than 10 minutes.

SLA fit:
- With 6 GPUs and warmed KV caching, predicted p95 end-to-end: ~300–320 ms (within their 350 ms SLO).
- p99 tail expected ~650–750 ms in worst case (still under their preferred 800 ms).

Cost note (high level):
- 6x H100 reserved monthly commitment number in the attached spreadsheet; shows committed vs burst/overage economics and expected token unit price that we would propose in draft SLA.

I'll attach a short one-page summary and a spreadsheet with the cells so we can send to Samir. If Priyom wants to soften the committed slab to 4 GPUs with more aggressive fallback, we can create an alternate 'conservative' vs 'lean' offer.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-13T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed committed slab and SLA draft (LyricX)

Samir / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per the attached estimate and Karthik's calc, we recommend the following commitment to hit your p95 <350 ms SLO while giving headroom for short spikes:

Proposal summary:
- Committed slab: 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) running rw-infer-v2-13b-q4f16 for primary traffic.
- Canary + rollout: 10% traffic day 0 -> 50% day 1 -> 100% day 3 if metrics stable.
- SLA: p95 <350 ms (monthly uptime SLA for inference request surface), p99 <900 ms (best-effort), tokens/month included: 1.2B tokens/mo; overage token pricing tiered (see attachment).
- Fallback policy: automatic spill to rw-infer-v2-7b-q4 (hosted) when slab consumption >95% for >2 min OR when average queueing latency exceeds 80 ms.
- KV-cache warmup: we will pre-warm common prefixes during your daily release window and include a pre-warm run during rollout to reduce cold-start penalties.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, I'll upload an SLA doc with a small procurement appendix and a DocuSign link for the reservation contract.
2) Procurement: confirm billing contact and legal review timelines — typical lead time is ~7–10 business days for reserved slabs.
3) Engineering: Karthik recommended running a 48-hour synthetic replay against a staging slab; we can schedule this as soon as the contract is signed.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7654321
DocuSign (proposal): https://docusign.com/ABC-DocuSign-lyricx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the numbers.

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

2) Can you provide an optional 4-GPU lean plan with higher overflow and a cost delta so the execs can see a lower-commitment option?

If you can add both to the DocuSign packet, we'll try to push through legal + procurement next week.

Best,
Samir
